title: Private network MTU, certificate rotation, and fast rollback requirements (PRD)
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for Private/VPC deployments covering three tightly-related operational surface areas: (1) network MTU and packet fragmentation constraints for inference runtime and operator control plane, (2) certificate/key rotation workflows that must function in limited- or zero-egress (air-gapped) environments, and (3) operator-level fast rollback and canary detection targets to limit blast radius during upgrades.
context: Customers operating in isolated VPCs and air-gapped sites have reported intermittent packet fragmentation causing large KV-cache RPCs to fail, and lengthy certificate rotation procedures that require manual operator intervention. Separately, recent upgrades exposed a slow rollback path for operator-managed control-plane changes. This ticket consolidates requirements into a single PRD to guide engineering and SRE workstreams for runtime and operator improvements.
scope: Define MTU negotiation expectations between operator, node agents, and model-serving containers (minimum supported MTU 1400, explicit tests for 9000 do not block)
Specify transport behavior for large KV cache syncs and streaming token responses to tolerate fragmentation or avoid it via chunking
Design a certificate/key rotation flow that can perform signing and rotation using an on-prem KMS or pre-seeded signed artifacts without any outbound egress
Require operator rollback path that can revert operator-controlled control-plane changes within 2 minutes for targeted nodes, with a documented safe-state
Create acceptance criteria and automated tests (integration + chaos) to validate behavior under constrained network conditions and air-gapped upgrade scenarios
out_of_scope: Complete re-architecture of model-serving transport protocols (protocol-level redesign decisions are separate RFCs)
Customer-specific custom KMS integrations (this PRD defines the generic contract; specific integrations will be follow-ups)
End-to-end data residency and legal compliance review (handled by compliance team)
acceptance_criteria: Network: All control-plane RPCs (operator <-> node agent, node agent <-> runtime) succeed with MTU >= 1400; documented degradation behavior for MTU < 1400
Network: Large KV-sync and prefix cache transfers are chunked by default when runtime detects PMTU < 1500, no end-to-end request fails due to single-packet size

Certificate rotation: We provide two supported rotation modes: (A) online rotation with customer-managed KMS over TLS, and (B) offline rotation via signed rotation bundles (artifact format with signed metadata). Both modes must be automatable from the operator CLI without outbound network calls for mode B
Certificate rotation: Rotation bundle validation includes signed metadata (SHA256), expiry checks, and a dry-run verification path that can be executed on-airgap prior to activation

Rollback: The operator must be capable of rolling back a config or image change on a per-node or per-pool basis within 2 minutes (for single-node targets) and within 15 minutes for a full-pool rollback; rollback must restore previously healthy image and config and reapply necessary local state-migrations

Canary & detection: Telemetry must detect regressions (error rate spike, >2x baseline CPU, token latency p95 increase >30%) within 5 minutes of canary start and trigger automatic small-scale rollback when configured

Observability: All steps (rotation, upload/apply of rotation bundle, rollback execution) emit audit events to local logs and the control-plane audit stream; events are human-readable and include action, actor, timestamp, and pre/post state hashes

Testing: CI must include a suite that validates MTU-limited scenarios (simulate PMTU down to 1200), offline rotation bundle application, and rollback execution. Tests must run in the private-deploy E2E harness and pass on PRs touching operator/runtime glue code
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (dev): Implement runtime chunking and MTU-detection library; unit tests and local E2E harness verification
Stage 2 (canary): Deploy operator changes to internal canary VPC with simulated PMTU constraints and run telemetry-defined canaries
Stage 3 (customer pilots): Offer offline rotation bundle flow to two pilot customers in closed-network mode; collect feedback
Stage 4 (GA): Ship required CLI/operators docs, automated tests, and operator dashboard panels for rotation and rollback status
test_plan: Simulated PMTU tests: run suffix throughput and large-KV transfer tests with PMTU values {900, 1200, 1400, 1500}; assert no request-level failures at >=1400
Offline rotation bundle validation: generate signed bundle, apply in a fully-airgapped environment, verify node accepts and rotates certs without attempting outbound connections
Rollback timings: inject failing change in canary, measure median and 95th percentile time to rollback for single-node and pool-level targets
Chaos test: simulate packet loss (5-10%) and reordering during KV-sync and assert cache consistency and no crashes
risks: Incorrect chunking strategy could increase latency for small requests if not optimized
Customers with extremely constrained MTU (<1200) may require additional operator-side tuning or VPN configuration
Offline rotation bundles introduce operational complexity; poor UX may cause customer operators to delay rotations leading to expired certificates
security_considerations: Rotation bundle must be signed with a Redwood private key; verification must be strict (reject on any metadata mismatch)
All local audit logs capturing rotation and rollback must be tamper-evident (append-only file or write to secure journald/HSM-backed audit sink if present)
Operator CLI must require MFA and RBAC gate when performing pool-level rollbacks in production
open_questions: Should the default MTU floor be 1400 or 1280 (IPv6 minimum) for conservative compatibility?
Do we require offline bundle signing keys to be rotated on a schedule, and if so, who handles the key lifecycle in air-gapped sites?
What is the exact SLA for rollback when the control-plane itself is partially degraded?
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Decided to target MTU floor 1400 for initial delivery to balance compatibility and reduced fragmentation risk
2026-03-04: Chose two rotation modes (online KMS and offline signed bundle) to cover both connected and air-gapped customers
2026-03-05: Rollback target set to 2 minutes for single-node, 15 minutes for pool-level; engineering requested addition of automated dry-run prior to rollout
